fact: The BCEAO communique of 2 October 2026, for the whole WAEMU, sets binding terms for person-to-person e-money transfers through PI-SPI, taking effect on 2 November 2026 (free sends up to FCFA 8,000 a day, 0-0.8% above, free receipt).

The BCEAO decided that from 2 November 2026 interoperable e-money transactions within WAEMU must be made through the PI-SPI platform, covering transfers between bank or microfinance accounts and accounts at e-money institutions or payment establishments.

iAfrikan reports the BCEAO told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution in the eight WAEMU countries, Togo included, in April 2026 to be connected to PI-SPI by 30 June 2026, then on 25 June 2026 moved the deadline to 30 September 2026 (microfinance institutions to 30 June 2027).

Citing the UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 annual report, the article says Tmoney in Togo was licensed as an e-money institution (EME) in September 2025, among 18 licensed EMEs in the union at end-2025.

Citing the UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 report, the article says the number of licensed e-money issuers (EME) rose from 14 to 18 in 2025, with Tmoney in Togo among the new approvals (no month given; year of the report used).

Finance SAO reports a BCEAO communique of 25 June 2026 set 30 September 2026 as the deadline for banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions in WAEMU to integrate with PI-SPI (30 June 2027 for microfinance institutions); 9 authorised institutions were in Togo at 31 July 2026.
